newsitem.title: UK: Stimulated mice have more brain cells, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Stimulated mice have more brain cells, study finds.

text.p: Mice given toys to play with and large cages to explore have more brain cells than bored mice kept in tiny cages, U.S. researchers reported on Wednesday.
Fred Gage and colleagues at the Salk Institute in La Jolla, California found mice that lived in an "enriched environment" had 15 percent more brain cells than mice in standard cages.
Half the mice were kept in small cages like normal laboratory mice, while half were put in larger cages and given toys to play with.

When they killed the mice after a few months and looked at their brains they found that the "pampered" mice had more brain cells in the hippocampus -- the part of the brain associated with learning and memory. The pampered mice also showed "a moderate, though significant improvement" in a maze test.
Gage's group said no one yet understood what caused brain cells to grow, so it was not clear how an enriched environment could affect the process.
